To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chemical closure of stomatal pores in field-grown plants can reduce water loss from soil and increase water use efficiency by as much as 50%.
the use of a chemical that closes stomata can decrease water loss from a population of field-grown crops.

chemical closure of stomatal pores by the application of 1,1-dimethylpiperidinium chloride to the leaf surfaces of soybean plants in the field decreased soil water loss and increased the water content of the topsoil, but did not significantly increase the yield of soybean seeds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) The effect on transpiration of spraying a population of field plants with compounds that close stomata.

the effect of chemical closing of stomata on (1) transpiration of a population of plants growing in a field; (2) the water content of the topsoil and the water content of a population of roots in the soil; (3) the water content and dry-matter yield of the above-ground parts of the plants.
the effect of chemicals which close stomata on the transpiration of field-grown plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemical closure of stomatas in field crops is an effective way to decrease water loss.
the chemical closure of stomatas by a compound such as the one used in this study would decrease the transpiration from plants in the field by a significant amount.

the chemical treatment of field-grown maize plants with 2-chloroethyl phosphonic acid, a chemical which closes stomata and decreases transpiration, increased the water-use efficiency of these plants by increasing their dry-matter yield per unit of water transpired.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemical closure of stomatas reduces the transpiration rate of field plants.
the chemical treatment reduced the transpiration and the water use of a crop of maize plants growing in the field, but did not significantly affect the growth or yield of the crop.
the stomatal closure induced by the compounds was sufficient to reduce transpiration of the plants by 50 per cent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical is effective in decreasing the water use of plants in the soil, and it is effective at a low dosage rate of 0.5 mg. per square foot of soil.
the use of chemical compounds that close stomata may be useful in decreasing the water loss from plants in the field and in increasing the efficiency of water utilization by plants.
the chemical compounds we used are effective in reducing transpiration of plants growing in the field.
